hannah: Running through the quickstart in a disposable Docker dev image. `redwoodctl login --profile sample` crashes when saving the profile. It used to work but recent package update started failing on CI.

hannah: Error: 
error: failed to save profile: write /workspace/.config/redwood/profiles.json: permission denied
failed to replace file atomically: permission denied

hannah: Repo is mounted from host and owned by uid 1000, container runs as uid 1001. Workaround is export XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/foo, but that's not great for onboarding.

jon: We see this with NFS/shared workspaces too. Atomic rename across mounts returns EXDEV or EACCES. We should fall back to a safe write mode automatically.

mia: Also the device-code auth is flaky in these environments. TTL is 60s. During workshops folks take >60s to switch devices and copy/paste, then the CLI errors out with "device code expired" and doesn't provide a simple retry flow.

hannah: I proposed an --in-memory flag so login won't try to persist in CI; CLI would print the token and a small command to persist later, e.g. `redwoodctl persist --path /tmp/token.json`. That'd speed sample-app onboarding without changing host FS.

nico: Good ideas. Proposed features: --in-memory (no write, prints token), --persist <path> (explicit path), automatic fallback when rename returns EXDEV to copy+unlink, and detect CI env vars (CI=1, GITHUB_ACTIONS) to prefer non-atomic writes. Also add --device-ttl-seconds and --headless-token /path for pre-authorized tokens in CI.

junior-dev: +1 for clickable device URL when TERM supports it. Reduces copy/paste errors in demos.

ci-bot: (automated) workflow failed: onboarding-quickstart  auth: write permission to config. logs: https://ci.internal/runs/555

hannah: I'll attach a tiny Dockerfile and repro script to the GH issue. Short-term: update onboarding docs with explicit XDG_CONFIG_HOME recipe and a note about device TTL. Medium-term: implement in-memory/persist flags and EXDEV fallback.
